messages:
Ava: Hey team  I started a focused PR to add a short-sequence section to the Optimize toolkit page (prefetch + quant profiles + a canary rollout recipe). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/863
Jon: Thanks. Can you include a public-safe Python helper instead of linking the internal repo? Ops doesn't want private links in docs.
Ava: Yep, I'll extract a minimal helper and add it under /examples/docs/prefetch_shortseq.py. Draft snippet in the PR for now.
Priya: Quick UX ask  make the migration steps explicit: pre-check -> canary -> monitor -> scale. People skim docs; they need a checklist.
Ava: Added a collapsible checklist (Pre-checks / Canary rollout / Post-verify). Canary JSON I added: 
```json
{"canary_steps": ["10%","40%","100%"], "monitors": ["latency_p95","error_rate","token_cost"]}
```
Marcus: On the quant profile examples: please call out that q4_1 behaves poorly for extremely short prompts (<32 tokens) on some models. Suggest fallback to fp16 or use q8_0 for <32 tokens.
Ava: Noted. I added a short table and a one-liner: "For <32-token traffic consider q8_0 or fp16 fallback; measure exact-match and latency delta."
Jon: Can we add a tiny JS SDK example showing batching + prefetch toggled off for cold-starts? Many front-end folks copy JS more than py.
Ava: Added JS snippet and a comment about SDK versions: "uses SDK >=0.10.0; BatchClient renamed in 0.10.0".
Priya: Also include the SQL-ish query we use in console to detect token alignment drift: `SELECT sample_id, alignment_pct FROM evals WHERE profile='short_seq' ORDER BY alignment_pct ASC LIMIT 50` (pseudo).
docs-bot: @Ava created ticket JIRA-OPT-412: docs: add public prefetch helper + canary recipe :bell:
Marcus: FYI the Go snippets in the PR reference `BatcherV2`. For older customers we should show compatibility note for v0.9.x.
Ava: Good catch  I added a compatibility footnote and a tiny migration snippet: `if sdk_version < "0.10.0": use BatchClientV1`
Jon: Minor nit  the rollout percentages are aggressive for some teams. Maybe suggest a conservative variant in the checklist (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) and label it "low-risk".
Ava: Added both conservative and standard recipes and labeled them. Also added recommended monitors to wire into the Console alerts: token_cost delta, latency_p95, and exact-match regression.
Priya: Will run a quick language pass and check anchors/redirects after Marcus signs off on the tech bits.
Marcus: I'll review quant wording tonight. If no blockers, we can merge Thursday morning. I'll leave inline comments in the PR.
Ava: Thanks! Also added a tiny script in examples to synthesize a 2k-sample prompt set for validating p95/p99.
Jon: One more thing  please add a one-line to release notes: "Docs: Optimize toolkit 1 short-sequence prefetch & canary rollout guidance" so PMs can call it out.
Ava: Done in the release notes draft. TY all :shipit:
